builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CRAFT-AI: Capability and Requirement Alignment for Flexible Manufacturing through Agentic AI
summary: The method replaces manual translation of natural-language production requirements into manufacturing configurations and Asset Administration Shell instances by a tool-using LLM agent backed by a library of twelve reference Factory I/O scenes. Cost is modest in compute (an API or single-GPU LLM call suffices) but substantial in engineering effort: curating AAS capability descriptions and reference implementations is a prerequisite. It fails silently when domain knowledge is incomplete unless safeguards surface gaps, as shown by the task where a wrong sensor selection only surfaced through explicit risk communication; correctness beyond five toy tasks is unverified.
rationale: The approach is a domain-specific agentic engineering prototype validated only on twelve reference scenes and five tasks, so it is worth tracking for manufacturing-automation teams but not ready for production adoption or small-scale testing without the surrounding AAS knowledge base.

claims.statement: The method replaces manual translation of natural-language production requirements into manufacturing configurations and Asset Administration Shell instances by a tool-using LLM agent backed by a library of twelve reference Factory I/O scenes. Cost is modest in compute (an API or single-GPU LLM call suffices) but substantial in engineering effort: curating AAS capability descriptions and reference implementations is a prerequisite. It fails silently when domain knowledge is incomplete unless safeguards surface gaps, as shown by the task where a wrong sensor selection only surfaced through explicit risk communication; correctness beyond five toy tasks is unverified.

On four valid task descriptions the agent generated proper requirements, correct references, correct components, and valid Factory I/O scenes; on a fifth task with missing knowledge it flagged gaps and an incompatible sensor. No quantitative comparison is reported.
